$comment: Build config for 'Care Circle' — aging-parent care coordination hub. Feed this to a build script that provisions the workspace via the Notion API. Requires API version 2025-09-03 or later (data-source model + Views API).

meta.note_on_build_order: Relations must be created after both sides exist. Build script should do two passes: pass 1 creates data sources with non-relation properties, pass 2 patches in relation and rollup properties.

databases.title: Providers & Contacts
databases.description: Every human or org involved in care. Doctors, pharmacy, home health agency, the neighbor with a spare key.

Login Notes.$comment: Where the credentials live — NOT the credentials themselves. Say this explicitly in the template copy.

databases.title: Care Team
databases.description: The people sharing the load. Drives expense splitting and coverage assignment.

Location.$comment: Distance matters. The out-of-state sibling can take on admin instead of visits.

Expense Share %.$comment: Defaults to equal split; families often weight by income or proximity.

Balance.$comment: Positive = owed money. Negative = owes money. Surface this prominently.

databases.title: Conditions & Allergies
databases.description: Standing medical facts. Feeds the ER sheet.

databases.title: Medications
databases.description: Current and discontinued. The discontinued history matters — doctors ask what's been tried.

Refill Alert.expression: if(and(prop("Status") == "Active", prop("Days to Refill") <= 7), "⚠️ Refill soon", "")

views.name: ER Sheet — Current Meds
views.$comment: This is the printable one. Keep columns to: Medication, Dose, Frequency, Purpose, Prescriber.

databases.title: Care Log
databases.description: Dated observations. The single most valuable database here — it turns 'Mom seems worse lately' into evidence a doctor can act on, and documents the timeline for care-level decisions.

views.name: Flagged for Next Visit
views.$comment: Walk into the appointment with this open.

views.name: Trend
views.$comment: Shows escalation over months. Powerful in a family conversation about moving to assisted living.

databases.title: Appointments
databases.description: Before-and-after structure. The 'Questions to Ask' field prevents the classic failure where you leave the office having forgotten the one thing you meant to raise.

databases.title: Coverage Schedule
databases.description: Who's got which day. Solves the 'I thought you were going Thursday' problem.

views.name: Unclaimed
views.$comment: The guilt-free ask. Nobody has to text the group chat.

databases.title: Shared Expenses
databases.description: Running tally. Prevents the slow resentment build that wrecks sibling relationships.

Tax Deductible?.$comment: Medical expenses for a dependent parent may be deductible. Include a note pointing to IRS Pub 502 — and a clear line that this isn't tax advice.

databases.title: Key Documents & Accounts
databases.description: Where things live. Not the documents themselves — the map to them.

Account/Policy Number.$comment: Warn users in template copy: Notion is not a password manager. Store last-4 only, or a pointer to where the full number lives.

views.name: Gaps
views.$comment: Most families discover here that there's no healthcare proxy. That realization alone is worth the purchase price.

pages.title: 🚨 Emergency Sheet
pages.description: The print-and-go page. Design for one sheet of paper, black and white, readable at arm's length.

blocks.text: Print this. Keep a copy in the car, in the go-bag, and on the fridge. Update after every med change.
Patient
Name / DOB / Address / Insurance ID / Medicare number
In an Emergency, Call
Healthcare proxy name + phone, then backup
Allergies & Conditions
Current Medications
Advance Directive
DNR status and where the signed document is located
Start here → Setup Guide
This Week
Needs Attention
Recent Observations

pages.title: Setup Guide
pages.description: 15-minute onboarding. Ordered by urgency, not by database. Buyers who finish setup don't refund.

blocks.text: Add everyone to Care Team (5 min)
Enter current medications from the pill bottles (10 min) — this alone is worth doing today
Add primary doctor and pharmacy to Contacts
Fill in the Emergency Sheet header and print it
Audit Key Documents — mark what's missing
Share this page with siblings (Share → Invite)
Everything else can wait. Come back to Coverage and Expenses when you're ready.

pages.title: Hard Conversations Prep
pages.description: Content page, not a database. High perceived value, zero build cost, and it's what makes this feel like a product rather than a spreadsheet.

blocks.text: Talking about giving up the car keys
Raising assisted living without a fight
Questions to ask before choosing a facility
Splitting the load when one sibling does everything
What to ask at a first neurology appointment

build_notes.gallery_views: The Views API currently rejects gallery type — build any gallery views manually in the UI after the script runs.
build_notes.database_templates: Add these by hand: a 'New Appointment' template pre-filled with the Questions to Ask structure, and a 'Daily Check-In' care log template. API support is limited and these matter a lot for usability.
build_notes.privacy_copy: Include a visible disclaimer page: this is not HIPAA-covered storage, don't put SSNs or passwords in it, and it isn't medical or legal advice. Protects you and builds trust.
build_notes.lite_version: Free tier = Emergency Sheet + Medications + Contacts only. That's the lead magnet. It's genuinely useful alone, and the gap to the paid version is obvious the moment a second sibling gets involved.
